The veteran wideout has caught 19 passes for 214 yards and a touchdown through three games while outproducing both Rome Odunze and Luther Burden III. Raymond will be a solid fantasy option in Week 4 against the Jets.

news.body: Kalif Raymond caught all five of his targets for 40 yards in the Bears' 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2.
news.head: Kalif Raymond catches five passes in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Raymond continues to make the most of solid involvement in the Chicago passing attack to begin the season, recording five or more receptions in each of the first two games. The wideout continues to take advantage of his familiarity with head coach Ben Johnson's offense, with a Week 3 contest against the Philadelphia Eagles up next.

news.body: Kayshon Boutte caught 3-of-5 targets for 38 yards in the Texans 26-3 win over the Titans.
news.head: Kayshon Boutte catches three passes Sunday
news.impact: Boutte remains off the fantasy radar in his current role, especially with the Texans trading for Marvin Harrison Jr.

news.body: Kayshon Boutte caught 3-of-4 targets for 36 yards in the Texans 34-30 loss against the Cowboys.
news.head: Kayshon Boutte catches three passes Sunday
news.impact: Boutte remains off the fantasy radar in his current role in the Texans wide receiver room.

news.body: Kayshon Boutte caught both of his targets for 21 yards in a 19-17 loss to the Colts.
news.head: Kayshon Boutte hauls in two passes in Week 3
news.impact: Boutte continues to struggle to carve out a clear role in the Houston offense, even with Nico Collins (hamstring) out of the lineup. The 24-year-old will look to improve on his season long numbers in a Week 4 matchup against a banged up Dallas' secondary.

news.body: Kayshon Boutte caught 3-of-5 targets for 37 yards in the Texans 20-6 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.head: Kayshon Boutte catches three passes Sunday
news.impact: Boutte continues to learn the playback in his second game with the Texans. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role as an upside WR4/WR5.

news.body: KC Concepcion Jr. (concussion) took part in Wednesday's practice session.
news.head: KC Concepcion Jr. (concussion) practices Wednesday
news.impact: Concepcion is in the concussion protocol, but Wednesday's activity certainly looks promising for his availability in Week 6. If Concepcion cannot go, Jerry Jeudy and Isaiah Bond will see more snaps.

news.body: KC Concepcion (head) has been ruled out for the remainder of the Browns game against the Jets on Sunday after a dirty hit from Minkah Fitzpatrick.
news.head: KC Concepcion (head) ruled out for remainder of Sunday
news.impact: Fitzpatrick had ripped off KC’s helmet previously before targeting his head while the rookie was making a grab. He most certainly has a concussion, and will likely be questionable for next weeks game. Denzel Boston will headline the Browns receiver group with KC out, with Jerry Jeudy seeing additional snaps.

news.body: KC Concepcion Jr. secured 5-of-8 targets for 64 yards in Thursday's 27-24 win over the Steelers.
news.head: KC Concepcion Jr. hauls in five passes Thursday night
news.impact: After managing to catch just two of his nine targets in Week 3, Concepcion bounced back with a new career high in receiving yards Thursday night. Concepcion has quickly carved out his role in the Browns' offense, as the rookie is tied for the team lead with 17 receptions through four games. He's averaged only 8.5 yards on those catches with a long of 21 and has yet to find the end zone. Still, he is a decent play in deeper PPR formats.

news.body: KC Concepcion Jr. caught 2-of-9 targets for just nine yards in Sunday's 21-18 win over the Carolina Panthers.
news.head: KC Concepcion Jr. quiet in win Sunday
news.impact: The rookie was targeted a team-high nine times on Sunday, but he was only able to catch two of those targets for just nine yards in a win over the Panthers. He doesn't project to have consistent fantasy value for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Keenan Allen (rest) missed Indianapolis' practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Keenan Allen (rest) misses practice Wednesday
news.impact: Allen was given the day off on Wednesday as a veteran rest day. He seems to be over his groin injury now, so fantasy managers should expect him to play in full in Week 6, and he will also see more work than usual if Josh Downs (rest/hamstring) is sidelined against the Titans this week.

news.body: Keenan Allen caught five of nine targets for 45 yards in the Colts' 34-22 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
news.head: Keenan Allen snags five passes in loss
news.impact: Allen was able to PPR his way into a semi-usable day, nothing fantastic, but didn't leave you hanging. He's a bit up and down at this point in his career, and he lacks any sort of ceiling, making him a floor play at best.

news.body: Colts WR Keenan Allen (groin) is officially active for a Week 5 matchup with the Steelers.
news.head: Keenan Allen (groin) officially active for Week 5
news.impact: Allen continues to deal with a nagging groin injury, but is cleared to suit up against Pittsburgh. With Allen active, Darius Slayton is a healthy inactive.

news.body: Keenan Allen (groin) is officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
news.head: Keenan Allen (groin) officially questionable for Sunday
news.impact: Allen is still dealing with a groin injury and will be questionable to play heading into the weekend. If he's ruled out ahead of game time, fantasy managers should expect more work for Darius Slayton (knee) against the Steelers this week.

news.body: Kendrick Bourne hauled in 5-of-8 targets for 70 yards in Sunday's 45-21 loss to the Detroit Lions.
news.head: Kendrick Bourne leads team in receiving Sunday
news.impact: Bourne was a bright spot for the Cardinals on Sunday. He led the team with 70 total receiving yards over the course of the game, although he wasn't able to get into the end zone at all, so his fantasy total remained mediocre. He will continue to be a highly involved member of this passing game moving forward with Marvin Harrison Jr. now out of town for the Cardinals.

news.body: Kendrick Bourne did not log a single target or touch in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Kendrick Bourne fails to log catch Sunday
news.impact: The veteran was entirely uninvolved on Sunday. He didn't register even a single target against the Giants, so he logged a big goose egg as far as fantasy scoring is concerned. He is not expected to be fantasy relevant at any point for the remainder of the season.

news.body: Kendrick Bourne caught 2-of-3 targets for 22 yards in the Cardinals 36-30 loss against the 49ers on Sunday.
news.head: Kendrick Bourne catches two passes Sunday
news.impact: Bourne has not been as involved the past two weeks after a big Week 1 performance. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

news.body: Kendrick Bourne caught 2-of-3 targets for just 11 yards in Sunday's 31-7 loss to the Seattle Seahawks.
news.head: Kendrick Bourne quiet in loss Sunday
news.impact: Bourne came back down to earth in Week 2 after a stellar performance in Arizona's season opener a week before. He only caught two passes for 11 yards on Sunday, but Arizona's offense as a whole struggled in this matchup against Seattle, so there's a good chance that he will bounce back and have relevance as a depth piece in most leagues sometime in the near future.

news.body: Keon Coleman caught one of his two targets for a seven-yard touchdown in a 37-34 overtime win over the Rams in Week 5's Monday night game.
news.head: Keon Coleman catches TD in Week 5
news.impact: Coleman made his only catch count as he hauled in Josh Allen's lone touchdown pass late in the third quarter. It was still a disappointing game for Coleman, who was expected to see a larger target share with DJ Moore (shoulder) inactive. Coleman will be on the flex radar in fantasy in Week 6 vs. the Raiders if Moore isn't ready to return to the field.

news.body: Keon Coleman (ankle) practiced in a full capacity on Thursday.
news.head: Keon Coleman (ankle) practices in full Thursday
news.impact: Coleman was able to practice in a full capacity on Thursday. His ankle injury seems to be a non-issue, so fantasy managers shouldn't be concerned with his health moving forward. He will be primed for a large workload again this week if DJ Moore (shoulder) is unable to play against the Rams.

news.body: Keon Coleman caught 6-of-7 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown in the loss to the Patriots.
news.head: Keon Coleman hauls in a touchdown in Week 4
news.impact: Coleman found the end zone for the first time this season on a 34-yard touchdown reception in the fourth quarter. Coleman set a new season high in yardage and targets in the loss Sunday. Fantasy managers could see Coleman become a bigger part of the offense heading into Week 5 after this performance.

news.body: Keon Coleman (ankle) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the New England Patriots.
news.head: Keon Coleman (ankle) cleared to play Sunday
news.impact: Coleman was on Buffalo's injury report throughout the week due to an ankle issue that has been bothering him recently, but it's not a serious issue and he has been cleared to play through it in Week 4. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to get a large workload with DJ Moore (shoulder) also inactive, however.

news.body: Khalil Shakir caught all three of his targets for 80 yards in a 37-34 overtime win over the Rams in Week 5's Monday night game.
news.head: Khalil Shakir goes for 80 yards in Week 5 win
news.impact: Shakir led the Bills in receiving, doing most of his damage on a 57-yard catch early in overtime. Shakir now has 18 catches for 256 yards and no touchdowns through his team's first five games. He will be a flex option in fantasy heading into Week 6 vs. the Raiders.

news.body: Khalil Shakir caught 7-of-8 targets for 82 yards in the Bills loss to the Patriots.
news.head: Khalil Shakir hauls in seven passes in Week 4
news.impact: Shakir led the team in receptions and targets in the loss Sunday. All three marks are new season highs for Shakir, a potential positive sign for fantasy managers that have rostered him in a tough season. Shakir and the Bills will take on the Rams in Week 5.

news.body: Khalil Shakir caught one of his three targets for six yards in the Bills' 24-16 Week 3 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Khalil Shakir quiet in Week 3 win
news.impact: Shakir struggled to make an impact Sunday, finishing with less than three receptions for the first time in three contests. The wideout remains one of many risky pass-catching options in the Buffalo offense to this point, with a Week 4 matchup against the New England Patriots up next.

news.body: Khalil Shakir caught 3-of-6 targets for 38 yards in Thursday night's 41-31 win over the Detroit Lions.
news.head: Khalil Shakir totals 38 yards in win Thursday
news.impact: The veteran wideout wasn't very impactful on Thursday night, catching just three passes for 38 yards on a night where Buffalo's offense couldn't be stopped. He isn't expected to be a strong fantasy option for the foreseeable future, although he may be primed for more work than usual for a week or two if DJ Moore (shoulder) has to miss time.

news.body: Kyle Williams caught all three of his targets for 91 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots win over the Raiders.
news.head: Kyle Williams finds the end zone in Week 5 win
news.impact: Williams hauls in a 34-yard pass from Drake Maye early in the third quarter for his first touchdown of the season. This was Williams first contest of the season in which he logged more than one reception. Williams and the Patriots will take on the Jets in Week 6.

news.body: Kyle Williams caught 1-of-3 targets for 34 yards in Sunday's 35-6 blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
news.head: Kyle Williams held to one catch Sunday
news.impact: The young wideout got on the field on Sunday and was able to haul in one 34-yard pass against the Jaguars, but he wasn't able to do anything else in the team's blowout loss. It's nice to see him actually on the field for New England, but he doesn't project to have any fantasy value for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Kyle Williams did not record a single target or touch in Sunday's 38-10 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Kyle Williams silent in Week 18 win
news.impact: The rookie was a complete non-factor on Sunday, failing to record even a single target in the team's blowout win over Miami. He showcased a lot of talent throughout his first NFL season, but it remains to be seen if he will take the next step in in 2026 and play more than a supporting role for the Patriots.

news.body: Kyle Williams caught 3-of-5 targets for 20 yards in the Patriots 42-10 win over the Jets.
news.head: Kyle Williams hauls in three passes in Week 17 win
news.impact: Williams was expected to see a larger role in the offense coming into the week with Mack Hollins and Kayshon Boutte out of action. His five targets and three receptions all mark new season highs for the rookie wide receiver. He will look to build on this performance in Week 18 against Miami.

news.body: Ladd McConkey (foot) was officially limited at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Ladd McConkey (foot) officially limited Wednesday
news.impact: McConkey was unable to see any real action last week due to his foot issue. He was able to practice on Wednesday to start the week this week, but he remained limited due to the same injury. He may play through it in Week 6, but it's hard for fantasy managers to trust starting him at this point in the season, even if his health is improving.

news.body: Ladd McConkey (foot) is expected to take part in Los Angeles' practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Ladd McConkey (foot) expected to practice Wednesday
news.impact: McConkey didn't see any action in last week's game due to a foot issue, but he is expected to make his return to practice on Wednesday. He will likely be limited, but we won't know for sure until sometime after practice. He will be hard to start in Week 6 against a tough Chiefs' defense considering how bad Los Angeles' offense has been throughout the start of the season.

news.body: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said that Ladd McConkey is “working back in this week.”
news.head: Ladd McConkey (foot) 'working back this week'
news.impact: McConkey was active this past week, but he did not see the field. His status will need to be monitored the rest of this week.

news.body: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said Ladd McConkey was only available in an emergency scenario in Sunday's game against the Broncos.
news.head: Ladd McConkey (foot) was active Sunday, did not play a snap
news.impact: McConkey was active, but he did not play a snap. He'll need to be monitored in practice this week.

news.body: Laquon Treadwell caught two of eight targets for 34 yards in the Colts' 34-22 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
news.head: Laquon Treadwell sees eight targets in Week 5
news.impact: Treadwell had the second most targets on the team, behind the nine of Tyler Warren and Keenan Allen. However, he failed to convert on most of those attempts, although sometimes he was the closest target on throwaway throws by QB Daniel Jones, so the targets are slightly inflated. Still, he's not going to be doing much for fantasy, so it's best to leave him on waivers.

news.body: Laquon Treadwell caught 5-of-6 targets for 42 yards in the Colts win over the Commanders.
news.head: Laquon Treadwell hauls in five passes in Week 4 win
news.impact: Treadwell saw an increase in playing time with the Colts dealing with injuries to Alec Pierce and Keenan Allen. Fantasy managers should expect this to be an outlier, as Treadwell's playing time will diminish once Allen and Pierce return.

news.body: Laquon Treadwell caught three passes for 61 yards in Sunday night's 33-30 OT loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Laquon Treadwell racks up 61 yards Sunday
news.impact: The veteran stepped up on Sunday after Alec Pierce left the game due to a heel injury. Treadwell played well and racked up 61 yards on the night, though he still wasn't great from a fantasy perspective. He should be more involved moving forward but still shouldn't be rostered in most league formats.

news.body: Laquon Treadwell failed to catch his only target in the Colts' 41-23 Week 1 loss to the Baltimore Ravens.
news.head: Laquon Treadwell sees one target in Week 1
news.impact: Treadwell operated as more of an afterthought in the Indianapolis passing attack for head coach Shane Steichen, with a difficult Week 2 contest against the Kansas City Chiefs up next.

news.body: Luther Burden III hauled in four of his six targets for a team-leading 47 yards while also rushing four times for two yards in the Bears' 31-7 Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
news.head: Luther Burden III leads underwhelming passing offense in Week 5 loss
news.impact: Burden III has seen consistent involvement in the Chicago passing attack to begin the season, recording four or more receptions in four of five contests. The wideout remains one of the more stable pass-catching options for head coach Ben Johnson ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

news.body: Luther Burden III caught four of his six targets for 63 yards and added an 11-yard run in a 23-12 win over the Jets in Week 4.
news.head: Luther Burden III goes for 63 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Burden got off to a fast start, catching three of his four passes in the first quarter, but was held to just one catch the rest of the way. He has been trending up, but fantasy managers are still waiting for a blow-up game from the second-year receiver. He will be a high-end WR3 in fantasy in Week 5 vs. the Packers.

news.body: Luther Burden III caught seven of his 11 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown while adding a seven-yard rush in a 27-7 win over the Eagles in Week 3.
news.head: Luther Burden III finds the end zone in Week 3
news.impact: Burden found the end zone on an eight-yard pass from Case Keenum in the first quarter. The veteran wideout led the Bears in targets and receptions on Monday night, although Kalif Raymond topped him with 90 receiving yards. Burden has 15 catches for 156 yards and one touchdown through three games. He will be a solid fantasy option in Week 4 against the Jets.

news.body: Luther Burden III hauled in three of his seven targets for 32 yards in the Bears' 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in Week 2.
news.head: Luther Burden III sees seven targets in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Burden III has provided mixed results to begin the season, finishing with less than 50 receiving yards in one of the first two games. The wideout remains difficult to trust as part of an inconsistent Chicago offense early on, with a Week 3 contest against the Philadelphia Eagles up next.

news.body: Makai Lemon caught 5-of-7 targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 19-17 loss to the Jaguars.
news.head: Makai Lemon finishes with five receptions in Week 5
news.impact: Lemon caught 10 passes over the first four weeks of the season. The first-round rookie set a new career high with five receptions in Sunday's game. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) sidelined for the second straight game, the Eagles needed more out of their other wide receivers. Lemon helped out Sunday, but he's still yet to have a real breakout performance.

news.body: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-6 targets for 27 yards in Sunday's 24-20 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Makai Lemon underwhelming in loss Sunday
news.impact: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) was sidelined for the Eagles on Sunday, but the rookie still wasn't able to take advantage and ended up with just three catches for 27 yards against the Rams. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect much value out of Lemon for the foreseeable future after his slow start to the season.

news.body: Makai Lemon caught three of his four targets for 29 yards in a 27-7 loss to the Bears in Week 3.
news.head: Makai Lemon catches three passes in Week 3
news.impact: Lemon turned in his best game as a pro on Monday night, finishing third on the team in targets and second in catches. The rookie wideout has now caught seven passes for 38 yards through three games. He remains a bench stash in fantasy heading into Week 4 against the Rams.

news.body: Makai Lemon caught his lone target for a 14-yard gain while losing five yards on his only carry in a 24-20 win over the Titans in Week 2.
news.head: Makai Lemon sees one target in Week 2
news.impact: Lemon was quiet in the close win as Philly leaned on DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks in the passing attack. Lemon now has just four catches for nine yards through two games as he looks to carve out a larger role in the Eagles' offense. He will not be a recommended fantasy option in Week 3 against the Bears.

news.body: Malachi Fields caught both of his targets for 20 yards in the Giants' 27-27 tie with the Washington Commanders in Week 5.
news.head: Malachi Fields bottled up in Week 5
news.impact: Fields has made minimal impact in the New York passing attack to begin the season, finishing with less than 35 receiving yards in four of five contests. The pass-catcher remains difficult to trust in all formats ahead of a Week 6 contest with the New Orleans Saints.

news.body: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-3 targets for 52 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 36-24 win over the Arizona Cardinals.
news.head: Malachi Fields hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.impact: Fields looked pretty good on Sunday, finishing with over 50 yards and a touchdown en route to a nice win over the Cardinals. It looks like his rookie season is not yet a wash even with QB Jaxson Dart out of the lineup, but there still isn't a big expectation of fantasy success from the young wideout at this point in the season.

news.body: Malachi Fields caught two passes for 19 yards in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Tennessee Titans.
news.head: Malachi Fields catches two passes Sunday
news.impact: The rookie only caught two passes on Sunday, but considering the very low offensive output of New York's offense as a whole, it doesn't come as much of a surprise. He has flashed some talent over the first few weeks of the season, but his poor situation renders him an irrelevant fantasy option moving forward.

news.body: Malachi Fields hauled in 2-of-6 targets for 30 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
news.head: Malachi Fields hauls in two passes Monday
news.impact: The Giants were trying to get the rookie wideout the ball on Monday night, but he was only able to haul in two out of his six targets over the course of the game. He finished with just 30 yards and isn't expected to get much better over the next couple of weeks with QB Jaxson Dart (knee) seemingly set to miss some time for New York.

news.body: Malik Nabers hauled in 11 of his team-leading 20 targets for 121 yards and one touchdown in the Giants' 27-27 Week 5 tie with the Washington Commanders.
news.head: Malik Nabers dynamic in Week 5 tie with Commanders
news.impact: Nabers has caught fire in the New York passing attack of late, finishing with over 100 receiving yards and at least one touchdown in each of his last two games. The wideout offers head coach John Harbuagh one of the few explosive pass-catching options in the New York offense ahead of a Week 6 matchup with the New Orleans Saints.

news.body: Giants coach John Harbaugh said Malik Nabers will be “ready to play” on Sunday.
news.head: Malik Nabers (knee) will play Sunday
news.impact: Nabers is coming off a big performance last week against the Cardinals. He should remain in fantasy lineups this week.

news.body: Malik Nabers (knee) was officially a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Malik Nabers (knee) officially limited at practice Thursday
news.impact: Nabers was a non-participant at New York's practice on Wednesday due to a knee issue, but it doesn't seem to be a serious issue, as he was able to return and practice in a limited fashion on Thursday. It looks likely that he will play in Week 5, and fantasy managers shouldn't hesitate to start him if he gets full clearance to play against the Commanders on Sunday.

news.body: Malik Nabers resumed practicing on Thursday.
news.head: Malik Nabers (knee) returns to practice Thursday
news.impact: Nabers was back on the field after missing practice on Wednesday. He remains on track to be good to go on Sunday.

news.body: Malik Washington caught 6-of-8 targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 31-24 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.head: Malik Washington racks up 43 yards Sunday
news.impact: Washington was technically Miami's leading receiver on Sunday, but he accomplished that with just 43 yards on the day, so his fantasy total wasn't much better than anyone else's. He will continue to have a low ceiling on a week-to-week basis moving forward with how bad Miami's offense is.

news.body: Malik Washington caught five passes for 67 yards in Sunday's 15-10 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
news.head: Malik Washington leads team in receiving Sunday
news.impact: Washington played pretty well on Sunday, finishing with most of the team's receiving yards in their loss to the Vikings. He's one of their only competent receivers at this point, but he still shouldn't be started in most league formats for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Malik Washington hauled in five of his team-high 10 targets for 56 yards while also rushing twice for five yards in the Dolphins' 24-10 Week 3 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs.
news.head: Malik Washington sees seven touches in Week 3 loss to Chiefs
news.impact: Washington has made the most of steady involvement as part of an underwhelming Miami passing attack, posting over 40 receiving yards in each of the first three games. The wideout remains another risky option in a disappointing Dolphins offense to this point, with a Week 4 contest against a disruptive Minnesota Vikings defense up next.

news.body: Malik Washington secured 4-of-5 targets for 43 yards, adding four yards on one carry in Sunday's 35-13 loss to the 49ers.
news.head: Malik Washington grabs four passes in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Washington has now hauled in seven combined passes over the first two weeks for an average of 13.7 yards. His production to this point is likely an indicator of what to expect for the duration of the season in the Dolphins' anemic offensive attack.

news.body: Marvin Harrison Jr. (trade) will be available to play in Week 6, according to HC DeMeco Ryans.
news.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. will play Week 6
news.impact: Houston recently made a trade to acquire Harrison from the Cardinals, and he is already going to be ready to play in time for Sunday's game against the Jaguars. He is going to be on a snap count to some degree, so fantasy managers shouldn't trust starting him in his first game as a Texan this week, however.

news.body: Marvin Harrison Jr. has been traded to the Houston Texans, per a report that came out after the Texans win over the Titans.
news.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. headed to Houston
news.impact: Harrison had worn out his welcome in Arizona, and will now be reunited with his college QB. He will look to rebuild his value with his new team, and hopefully provide a viable No.2 target behind Nico Collins. As for the likes of Jaylin Noel, Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell, and the injured Jayden Higgins, this will certainly cap their ceilings.

news.body: Marvin Harrison Jr. is inactive for Week 5 for the Arizona Cardinals against the Detroit Lions.
news.head: Marvin Harrison Jr. inactive for Week 5
news.impact: Harrison Jr. will not suit up while a trade continues to be finalized for the wideout, with Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne to lead the wide receiver group against a dismal Lions defense Sunday.

news.body: The Cardinals are finalizing a deal to trade WR Marvin Harrison Jr.
news.head: Marvin Harrison Jr: Cardinals finalizing trade
news.impact: The Cardinals informed Harrison this morning that he will be inactive for Sunday’s game against the Lions as the details of the trade are finalized. It remains unclear as of now where he will be traded.

news.body: Matthew Golden hauled in six of his seven targets for 123 yards in the Packers' 31-7 Week 5 win over the Chicago Bears.
news.head: Matthew Golden surpasses 100 yards in Week 5 win
news.impact: Golden has seen steady involvement in the Green Bay passing attack to begin the season, recording over 90 receiving yards in three of the first five games. The wideout remains one of the more impactful pass-catching options for quarterback Jordan Love, with a Week 6 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys up next.

news.body: Matthew Golden caught three of his seven targets for 21 yards and a touchdown while adding a six-yard rush in a 17-14 win over the Buccaneers in Week 4.
news.head: Matthew Golden finds the end zone in Week 4
news.impact: Golden found the end zone on a two-yard pass from Jordan Love in the second quarter. The second-year wideout now has 18 catches for 274 yards and two touchdowns through four games. Golden sets up as a WR2 in fantasy heading into a Week 5 matchup against the Bears.

news.body: Matthew Golden caught 5 of 12 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown in the Packers' 35-14 loss to the Falcons on Thursday.
news.head: Matthew Golden snags touchdown in loss to Falcons
news.impact: Golden had several passes intended for him tipped by defensive backs after being undethrown, and another target where the DB committed a pass interference penalty. So, the five catches on 12 targets may not seem great; there is still context to be had. He is startable each week for the Packers.

news.body: Matthew Golden hauled in four of his six targets for a team-high 58 yards in the Packers' 20-17 Week 2 win over the New York Jets.
news.head: Matthew Golden leads pass-catchers in Week 2 win over Jets
news.impact: Golden has been one of the few bright spots in an underperforming Packers offense to begin the season, recording four or more receptions for over 50 receiving yards in each of the first two contests. The wideout will look for another impactful performance in a favorable Week 3 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

news.body: The Steelers placed WR Michael Pittman on injured reserve.
news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) placed on IR
news.impact: Pittman will miss at least the next four weeks. Roman Wilson and Germie Bernard should both step into bigger roles in the Steelers wide receiver room.

news.body: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Michael Pittman re-aggravated his foot injury and will miss multiple weeks.
news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) expected to miss multiple weeks
news.impact: It appears Pittman could be placed on injured reserve. He was seen on a scooter on Wednesday. Roman Wilson will continue to see more opportunity as the Steelers WR2, while Germie Bernard will see more opportunity behind him.

news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) was officially a limited participant at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. (foot) officially limited Wednesday
news.impact: The veteran is now dealing with a foot injury of some kind. He was officially limited because of it on Wednesday, but he was also seen moving around on a scooter in the locker room, which makes it seem like a long-shot that he will play this week. If he's sidelined, fantasy managers should look for Roman Wilson to continue to benefit from his absence for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Michael Pittman Jr. was seen on a scooter in the Steelers locker room.
news.head: Michael Pittman Jr. seen on scooter in Steelers locker room
news.impact: It appears to be a foot injury for Pittman. He has been off the fantasy radar when healthy in his current role in the Steelers offense.

news.body: Michael Wilson caught 4-of-7 targets for just 30 yards in Sunday's 45-21 loss to the Detroit Lions.
news.head: Michael Wilson underwhelming in loss Sunday
news.impact: Wilson wasn't able to do much on Sunday, totaling just 30 yards on four catches in a loss to the Lions. He should be the team's clear-cut WR1 moving forward moving forward with Marvin Harrison Jr. now out of town, but he's still subject to having some stinker performances on a week-to-week basis.

news.body: Michael Wilson brought in 7-of-13 targets for 95 yards in Sunday's 36-24 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Michael Wilson leads team in receiving Sunday
news.impact: The young wideout was one of the bright spots for the Cardinals on Sunday. He led the team with 95 yards over the course of the afternoon, and he continues to build on the success that he has already found in the first quarter or so of the season. He should continue to be a worthy starter in most fantasy league formats for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Michael Wilson caught 11-of-17 targets for 89 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals 36-30 loss against the 49ers on Sunday.
news.head: Michael Wilson hauls in 11 passes Sunday
news.impact: Wilson posted his biggest performance of the early season fresh off his contract extension this past offseason. He hauled in a touchdown from Jacoby Brissett in the third quarter. He profiles as a WR3 heading into next week against the Giants.

news.body: Michael Wilson caught two of seven targets for 18 yards in the Cardinals' 31-7 loss to the Seahawks on Sunday.
news.head: Michael Wilson sees seven targets in loss
news.impact: Wilson failed to connect with QB Jacoby Brissett in this game, and fantasy managers will be wishing for more after such a bad showing. He wil look to bounce back against the Niners next Sunday.

news.body: Mike Evans caught 7-of-10 targets for 113 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers 32-29 win over the Seahawks on Sunday.
news.head: Mike Evans explodes for huge day Sunday
news.impact: In one drive alone to end the third quarter and start the fourth quarter, Evans caught four passes for big gains and the two point conversion after a touchdown. He'll be a strong WR2 play next week against the Commanders.

news.body: Mike Evans is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Seahawks.
news.head: Mike Evans (ribs) off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Evans returned to practice on Friday. He will be a WR2 play for fantasy managers.

news.body: Mike Evans returned to practice on Friday.
news.head: Mike Evans (ribs) back at practice Friday
news.impact: Evans is back after he did not practice on Thursday. He is on track to play on Sunday against the Seahawks.

news.body: Mike Evans (ribs) missed San Francisco's practice on Thursday.
news.head: Mike Evans (ribs) misses practice Thursday
news.impact: Evans was downgraded to a non-participant at practice on Thursday after being limited on Wednesday. He was able to play through the injury last week, however, so he still projects to do the same again in Week 5.

news.body: Nico Collins caught 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards in the Texans 26-3 win over the Titans.
news.head: Nico Collins sees seven targets Sunday
news.impact: It wasn't a huge afternoon for Collins as Houston controlled the entire game. He will remain a WR1 next week against the Jaguars.

news.body: Nico Collins was limited in practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Nico Collins (rest) limited in practice Wednesday
news.impact: It was a day to begin the week for Collins. He remains a locked and loaded WR1 for fantasy managers.

news.body: Nico Collins caught 7-of-8 targets for 118 yards and two touchdowns in the Texans 34-30 loss against the Cowboys.
news.head: Nico Collins explodes in return Sunday
news.impact: Collins picked right up where he left off in his return from injury. He scored the first touchdown of the day for Houston and continued to dominate all afternoon despite the loss. He'll be a WR1 next week against the Titans.

news.body: Nico Collins (hamstring) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Dallas Cowboys.
news.head: Nico Collins (hamstring) good to go for Sunday
news.impact: Collins is set to make his return to the lineup on Sunday after missing the last two games due to a hamstring injury. Fantasy managers shouldn't hesitate to start him as often as he's healthy and on the field moving forward. His return will likely mean less work for Dalton Schultz and Xavier Hutchinson for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Parker Washington brought down 6-of-9 targets for 124 yards and a pair of touchdowns in Sunday's 19-17 win over the Eagles.
news.head: Parker Washington rebounds with huge performance in Week 5
news.impact: Washington eclipsed the 100-yard mark for the first time this season on Sunday, doubling his touchdown total for the season in the process. He looked every bit the part of a dynamic WR1 on Sunday. However, the Jaguars have a plethora of talented pass catchers, and QB Trevor Lawrence does tend to spread the ball around. Still, Washington is a potent fantasy option.

news.body: Parker Washington caught 1-of-3 targets for just seven yards in Sunday's 22-17 win over the Cincinnati Bengals.
news.head: Parker Washington held to one catch Sunday
news.impact: Washington had a total disappearing act on Sunday. He was held to just one catch for a measly seven yards against the Bengals after starting out the first three weeks of the season as a red-hot fantasy option. He should bounce back and return to being a quality starter very quickly, but seeing this kind of floor for the veteran was unexpected and not ideal for fantasy managers.

news.body: Parker Washington hauled in 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 35-6 win over the New England Patriots.
news.head: Parker Washington hauls in touchdown Sunday
news.impact: Washington was slightly underwhelming in terms of receptions and yardage on Sunday, but he was able to find the end zone against New England, which left him with a nice fantasy total once again. He has been very good to start the season and should continue to be started in nearly all leagues for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Parker Washington caught seven of his 12 targets for 98 yards in a 20-13 loss to the Broncos in Week 2.
news.head: Parker Washington goes for 98 yards in Week 2
news.impact: Washington led the Jacksonville receivers in all receiving categories while nearly reaching 100 yards in a tough matchup against Denver. The veteran has been excellent through the first two games of the season, posting 12 catches for 181 yards and a touchdown. Clearly the alpha in the Jacksonville receiving room, Washington will be a low-end WR1/high-end WR2 in Week 3 against the Patriots.

news.body: Puka Nacua caught 17 of his 24 targets for 138 yards and a touchdown while rushing twice for nine yards in a 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills in Week 5.
news.head: Puka Nacua draws 24 targets in Week 5 loss
news.impact: Nacua drew an insane 24 targets, putting him third all-time in a single game in the NFL behind only Brandon Marshall (28) and Chris Chambers (26). The veteran wideout also found the end zone on a two-yard pass from Matthew Stafford in the fourth quarter. Nacua now has 31 catches for 337 yards and one touchdown in just three games this season. He will be a top-three fantasy WR in Week 6 vs. the Cardinals.

news.body: Puka Nacua (groin) is off of the injury report heading into Week 5.
news.head: Puka Nacua (groin) off injury report for Week 5
news.impact: Nacua was able to make his return to the lineup last week and is now off of the injury report entirely heading into Week 5. Fantasy managers should have no hesitations starting him as a top-tier fantasy option moving forward.

news.body: Puka Nacua caught 9-of-12 targets for 125 yards and added one touchdown on the ground in Sunday's 24-20 win over the Philadelphia Eagles.
news.head: Puka Nacua stellar in return game Sunday
news.impact: The star wideout made his return to the lineup in Week 4 after missing a bit of time due to an injury of some kind. He looked great in his first game back, finishing with 125 receiving yards and a rushing touchdown in a narrow win over the Eagles. He will continue to be a must-start fantasy option moving forward.

news.body: Puka Nacua (groin) is expected to receive a full workload for the Los Angeles Rams against the Philadelphia Eagles Sunday according to Adam Schefter.
news.head: Puka Nacua (groin) planning on full workload Sunday
news.impact: Nacua has missed the last games due to groin and hip injuries, but seems poised for a return to a major role in the Los Angeles passing attack barring any setbacks for head coach Sean McVay against the Eagles Sunday.

news.body: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited at practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Quentin Johnston (chest) limited at practice Wednesday
news.impact: Johnston was not able to play last week due to a chest injury that he's dealing with. He was able to practice on Wednesday, however, which is a good sign that he will be back for Week 6. If he's active, he may see more work than usual if Tre' Harris (hamstring) or Ladd McConkey (foot) are ruled out for Sunday's game.

news.body: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Quentin Johnston will “probably be limited this week like last for the practice.”
news.head: Quentin Johnston (chest) expected to be limited in practice
news.impact: “We’ll see where he’s at the end of the week,” Harbaugh said. Johnston will have a chance to return in Week 6.

news.body: Quentin Johnston has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Broncos.
news.head: Quentin Johnston (chest) ruled out Sunday
news.impact: Johnston is dealing with a chest injury. Tre Harris becomes an intriguing WR3/flex play in deeper leagues.

news.body: Quentin Johnston (chest) was a limited participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Quentin Johnston (chest) limited participant Thursday
news.impact: A chest injury has left Johnston limited at two-straight practices to start the week. He may very well be left with an injury designation heading into the weekend, and Tre' Harris will be primed for more work if Johnston is unable to play this week.

news.body: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said Rashee Rice will not practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Rashee Rice (hamstring) will not practice Wednesday
news.impact: Rice got banged up before the bye week. His status will need to be monitored in practice the next couple of days.

news.body: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice is questionable to return against the Raiders with a hamstring injury.
news.head: Rashee Rice (hamstring) questionable to return
news.impact: Rice suffered the injury after a reception and hobbled off the field. Fantasy managers should expect the team to provide an update after halftime.

news.body: Rashee Rice hauled in seven of his team-high nine targets for 88 yards in the Chiefs' 24-10 Week 3 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Rashee Rice leads pass-catchers in Week 3 win over Dolphins
news.impact: Rice has heated up in the Kansas City offense of late, posting over 80 receiving yards in each of his last two contests. The wideout remains one of the more dynamic pass-catching options in the Chiefs passing attack moving forward, with a Week 4 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders up next.

news.body: Rashee Rice (knee) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Rashee Rice (knee) without injury designation for Sunday
news.impact: Rice's knee injury is nothing more than a minor issue at this point and won't affect his availability for Week 3. Fantasy managers should be starting him this week, though maybe expectations should be tempered for him after an underwhelming first two games of the season.

news.body: Rashid Shaheed caught 2-of-4 targets for 23 yards in the Seahawks 32-29 loss against the 49ers.
news.head: Rashid Shaheed catches two passes Sunday
news.impact: Shaheed remains off the fantasy radar in his current role. The Seahawks passing offense remains Jaxon Smith-Njigba or no one every week right now.

news.body: Rashid Shaheed caught 1-of-3 targets for 20 yards in the Seahawks 30-23 win over the Chargers. He also saw two carries for 33 yards and a touchdown.
news.head: Rashid Shaheed scores touchdown on ground Sunday
news.impact: With Jadarian Price on IR, Emanuel Wilson was the workhorse in the Seahawks backfield. Shaheed saw two traditional handoffs from Sam Darnold with one of them resulting in a 28-yard touchdown. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

news.body: Rashid Shaheed was a full participant in practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Rashid Shaheed (hip) logs full practice Wednesday
news.impact: Shaheed is a volatile WR4 with upside in his current role.

news.body: Rashid Shaheed hauled in two of his three targets for 14 yards in the Seahawks’ 33-31 Week 3 loss to the Washington Commanders.
news.head: Rashid Shaheed catches two passes in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Shaheed has made minimal impact in the Seattle offense to behind the season, finishing under 40 receiving yards in each of the first three contests. The wideout remains another risky pass-catching option to this point, with a Week 4 matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers up next.

news.body: Rashod Bateman was not at the start of practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Rashod Bateman not practicing Wednesday
news.impact: It is unclear what Bateman is dealing with. His status will need to be monitored on the injury report.

news.body: Rashod Bateman hauled in 5-of-6 targets for 62 yards in Sunday's 30-23 win over the Falcons.
news.head: Rashod Bateman leads Ravens in receiving yards Sunday night
news.impact: With Tyler Huntley at QB, Bateman recorded his second-highest catch and yardage totals of the season. Bateman finished second on the team behind Zay Flowers in receptions Sunday night, and he's now averaged four per game over the last four weeks. Bateman is also averaging 14.6 yards per catch with one touchdown on the season. He's firmly in the flex conversation going forward.

news.body: Rashod Bateman is off the injury report for Sunday's game against the Falcons.
news.head: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) off injury report Sunday
news.impact: Bateman is off the fantasy radar with Tyler Huntley starting for Baltimore.

news.body: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) was upgraded to a full participant at practice on Thursday.
news.head: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) upgraded to full participant Thursday
news.impact: Bateman was able to practice in a full capacity on Thursday after being limited by a shoulder injury on Wednesday. He should be good to go for Sunday night's game but doesn't project to be a good fantasy option against the Falcons, especially if QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) is sidelined for the Ravens.

news.body: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said WR Roman Wilson will not play in Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
news.head: Roman Wilson (finger) ruled out for Week 6
news.impact: Wilson is expected to miss multiple weeks. He is week-to-week for now.

news.body: Steelers WR Roman Wilson is expected to miss a “couple of weeks” after suffering a finger injury on Sunday against the Colts.
news.head: Roman Wilson (finger) expected to miss multiple weeks
news.impact: Wilson is seeking a second opinion after he was originally diagnosed with a dislocated finger. With Michael Pittman Jr. on IR, rookie Germie Bernard will step into a bigger role alongside Pat Freiermuth.

news.body: The Steelers have ruled out WR Roman Wilson for the remainder of the game against the Colts with a finger injury.
news.head: Roman Wilson (finger) ruled out
news.impact: Wilson will finish without a catch on one target Sunday. With Wilson out, Germie Bernard and DK Metcalf will serve as the two top pass catchers for Aaron Rodgers for the remainder of the game.

news.body: Roman Wilson caught 3-of-6 targets for 74 yards and a touchdown in Thursday's 27-24 loss to the Browns.
news.head: Roman Wilson scores again in Week 4
news.impact: Wilson has now scored in two straight weeks, as he's become a consistently reliable target for QB Aaron Rodgers. Wilson has gotten exactly six targets in each of the first four games of the season, catching at least three of them each time out. Overall, he's second on the team with 188 receiving yards and tied for second with 14 receptions. Wilson should be fairly popular pickup in Week 5.

news.body: Rome Odunze hauled in three of his team-leading nine targets for 40 yards with a fumble lost in the Bears' 31-7 Week 5 loss to the Green Bay Packers.
news.head: Rome Odunze sees nine targets in Week 5 loss
news.impact: Odunze has struggled to make a consistent impact in the Chicago passing attack, finishing with less than 60 receiving yards in four of five contests. The wideout remains a risky pass-catching option in all formats ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

news.body: Rome Odunze caught six of his seven targets for 94 yards in a 23-12 win over the Jets in Week 4.
news.head: Rome Odunze goes for 94 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Odunze led the Bears in all receiving categories in what was his best game of the season. The veteran receiver has now caught 14 passes for 233 yards and no touchdowns through four games. Odunze will be a low-end WR3 in fantasy in Week 5 vs. the Packers.

news.body: Rome Odunze caught three of his six targets for 44 yards in a 27-7 win over the Eagles on Monday night.
news.head: Rome Odunze goes for 44 yards in Week 3
news.impact: Odunze finished third on the Bears in targets and receiving yards but he was unable to find the end zone for the third straight game. The veteran wideout has been outproduced by both Luther Burden III and Kalif Raymond this season, catching just eight passes for 139 yards thus far through three games. He will be a fantasy flex option in Week 4 against the Jets.

news.body: Rome Odunze caught three of his four targets for 43 yards in the Bears' 9-3 Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.
news.head: Rome Odunze catches three passes in Week 2 loss
news.impact: Odunze has struggled to make an impact in a slow-starting Chicago passing attack to begin the season, finishing with three receptions or less in each of the first two games. The pass-catcher remains difficult to trust with the potential absence of quarterback Caleb Williams ahead of a Week 3 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.

news.body: Romeo Doubs caught 1-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Patriots win over the Raiders Sunday.
news.head: Romeo Doubs quiet in Week 5 win
news.impact: Doubs saw a massive reduction in targets Sunday, dropping from nine in the win over the Bills last week. Drake Maye and the Patriots still passed the ball well, but Doubs did not factor into the offense. The veteran will look to bounce back against the Jets in Week 6.

news.body: Romeo Doubs caught 6-of-9 targets for 58 yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots win over the Bills.
news.head: Romeo Doubs hauls in two touchdowns in Week 4 win
news.impact: Doubs caught passes of two and 14 yards to account for two of Drake Maye's three touchdown passes on the day. This was easily Doubs' best day as a Patriot. Fantasy managers should expect Doubs to continue to see plenty of targets heading into a Week 5 matchup with Las Vegas.

news.body: Romeo Doubs caught 3-of-4 targets for 49 yards in Sunday's 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars.
news.head: Romeo Doubs underwhelming in loss Sunday
news.impact: Doubs looked good with nearly 100 yards in Week 2, but he didn't find the same success this week, catching just three passes for 49 scoreless yards in a blowout loss to the Jaguars. He isn't a reliable fantasy option at this point in the season and shouldn't be started in most leagues, even if he continues to have decent upside on a week-to-week basis.

news.body: Patriots WR Romeo Doubs caught 3-of-4 targets for 96 yards in the Patriots' 20-3 win over the Steelers.
news.head: Romeo Doubs rebounds after a tough Week 1
news.impact: Doubs had a rough Week 1 but bounced back to lead the Patriots' wide receivers in yardage in Week 2, including an impressive 63-yard reception. With A.J. Brown on injured reserve, Doubs has the opportunity to lead the Patriots' wide receiver room until he returns. Doubs and the Patriots will travel to Jacksonville in Week 3.

news.body: Ryan Flournoy caught three of four targets for 90 yards in the Cowboys' 24-16 loss to the Bucs on Thursday.
news.head: Ryan Flournoy goes for 90 yards in loss
news.impact: Flournoy stepped in and made some big plays while operating as the Cowboys' WR2/3 on Thursday with CeeDee Lamb in and out of the lineup due to injury. If Lamb or George Pickens were to miss any time, Flournoy would be a primary pickup.

news.body: Ryan Flournoy caught 4-of-5 targets for 37 yards in the Cowboys 34-30 win over the Texans on Sunday.
news.head: Ryan Flournoy hauls in four passes Sunday
news.impact: Flournoy continues to have a limited role in the offense for Dallas. He is a WR4 for fantasy managers.

news.body: Ryan Flournoy caught two of his eight targets for 22 yards in a 34-31 loss to the Ravens in Brazil in Week 3.
news.head: Ryan Flournoy draws eight targets in Week 3
news.impact: Flournoy didn't do much damage through the air but he drew an encouraging eight targets in the loss. If he can continue to get that type of work consistently, Flournoy might work his way into the flex conversation in fantasy leagues. For now, he's best left on the bench heading into a Week 4 matchup against a tough Houston Texans defense.

news.body: Ryan Flournoy caught 5-of-6 targets for 23 yards in the Cowboys win over the Commanders.
news.head: Ryan Flournoy hauls in five passes in Week 2
news.impact: Flournoy continues to operate as the WR3 in the Cowboys' offense. Fantasy managers could view him as a flex play in deeper leagues heading into Week 3.

news.body: Stefon Diggs has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants.
news.head: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) ruled out Sunday
news.impact: Diggs remained absent from practice on Friday. Terry McLaurin was back at practice, but his status also remains up in the air heading into the weekend.

news.body: Stefon Diggs remained away from practice on Friday.
news.head: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) not at practice Friday
news.impact: Diggs is trending towards being ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants.

news.body: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) was officially a non-participant at practice again on Thursday.
news.head: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) officially a non-participant Thursday
news.impact: The veteran is still recovering from a hamstring injury and was officially a non-participant at practice again on Thursday, despite being present. It looks like he's trending the wrong way for Week 5, and his absence would significantly hurt the fantasy value of QB Jayden Daniels (elbow) ahead of a divisional matchup against the Giants on Sunday.

news.body: Stefon Diggs returned to practice on Thursday.
news.head: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) back at practice Thursday
news.impact: Diggs opened the week missing practice on Wednesday. He appears likely to be good to go, while Terry McLaurin remained sidelined from practice.

news.body: Tank Dell (knee) practiced in a full capacity on Wednesday.
news.head: Tank Dell (knee) practices in full Wednesday
news.impact: Dell was able to practice in a full capacity on Wednesday and continues to draw closer and closer to a return from a knee injury that has left him sidelined for a significant amount of time. He could play this week, but that isn't likely to be determined until sometime after practice on Friday.

news.body: Tank Dell has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Titans.
news.head: Tank Dell (knee) ruled out Sunday
news.impact: Dell returned to practice this week. He'll be activated within the next two weeks.

news.body: Tank Dell (knee) was limited at practice again on Thursday.
news.head: Tank Dell (knee) limited again Thursday
news.impact: Dell was limited for a second-straight practice on Thursday. That's a good sign that he will be back on the field sooner rather than later, but we won't know his official status for Week 5 until sometime after practice on Friday.

news.body: Tank Dell was limited in practice on Wednesday.
news.head: Tank Dell (knee) limited in practice Wednesday
news.impact: Dell was designated to return to practice on Wednesday. He is unlikely to return in Week 5. He has 21 days to officially be activated.

news.body: Tee Higgins caught 2-of-4 targets for just 22 yards in Sunday's 31-24 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Tee Higgins disappoints in win Sunday
news.impact: Higgins was dealing with several different injuries at practice throughout the week, but the team cleared him to play for Sunday's game. He didn't end up producing well, finishing with just 22 scoreless yards on two catches in a win over the Dolphins. He should have a good opportunity to get healthy during Cincinnati's bye week this week, however, so fantasy managers should expect him to bounce back after that.

news.body: Tee Higgins (groin/neck) will play for the Cincinnati Bengals against the Miami Dolphins Sunday according to Adam Schefter.
news.head: Tee Higgins (groin/neck) will play Sunday
news.impact: Higgins is good to go after entering the weekend with a questionable designation, joining Ja’Marr Chase (concussion) back in the Cincinnati passing attack against the Dolphins Sunday.

news.body: Tee Higgins is listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the Dolphins.
news.head: Tee Higgins (groin/neck) listed questionable Sunday
news.impact: Higgins was able to get in some work during practice on Friday. His status will have to be monitored closer to kickoff on Sunday.

news.body: Tee Higgins is now running some routes with the Bengals in individual drills during practice on Friday.
news.head: Tee Higgins (groin/neck) now running routes in individual drills
news.impact: Higgins was not going through the stretch period to begin practice. His status will need to continue to be monitored.

news.body: Terry McLaurin hauled in each of his four targets for a team-leading 62 yards in the Commanders' 27-27 Week 5 tie with the New York Giants.
news.head: Terry McLaurin leads pass-catchers in Week 5 tie with Giants
news.impact: McLaurin has heated up of late, recording 50 or more receiving yards in each of his last three contests. The wideout remains one of the more reliable options in the Commanders offense for head coach Dan Quinn, with a Week 6 matchup against the San Francisco 49ers up next.

news.body: Commanders WR Terry McLaurin (hamstring) is officially active for a Week 5 matchup with the Giants.
news.head: Terry McLaurin (hamstring) officially active for Week 5
news.impact: McLaurin was considered a game-time decision, but he was cleared to play after pregame warmups. The Commanders are without Stefon Diggs (hamstring) so McLaurin's return to the lineup will be a much needed boost.

news.body: Terry McLaurin remains a game-time decision for Sunday's game against the Giants.
news.head: Terry McLaurin (hamstring) remains game-time decision Sunday
news.impact: Keim notes that at this point, there's a slight lean to McLaurin playing, but it’s "just slight." His status will need to be monitored 90 minutes before kickoff.

news.body: Terry McLaurin is expected to be a game-time decision for Sunday's game against the Giants.
news.head: Terry McLaurin (hamstring) to be game-time decision Sunday
news.impact: McLaurin was able to return to practice on Friday. It is unclear how much he was able to do. The Commanders already ruled out Stefon Diggs for Sunday.

news.body: Tetairoa McMillan collected 14 receptions on 16 targets for 192 yards and a pair of touchdowns in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
news.head: Tetairoa McMillan shreds Lions secondary Sunday night
news.impact: For those frustrated by McMillan's paltry output in Week 3, the second-year star erupted for career highs in receptions and yards Sunday night. He also recorded the second multi-touchdown game of his career. It's important to note that this performance came with both Jalen Coker (quad) and Xavier Legette (knee) out, but McMillan still displayed his immense upside. He's a solid WR2 for fantasy purposes at present.

news.body: Tetairoa McMillan caught 2-of-5 targets for just 17 yards in Sunday's 21-18 loss to the Cleveland Browns.
news.head: Tetairoa McMillan disappears in loss Sunday
news.impact: McMillan got shut down on Sunday. He was only able to catch two passes for just 17 yards against the Browns, despite being the team's clear WR1 after Jalen Coker (quad) left the game. He should bounce back in the near future, but it's possible that his week-to-week floor will be lower than managers hoped coming into the season.

news.body: Tetairoa McMillan caught 5 of 10 targets for 101 yards in the Panthers' 34-3 win over the Falcons on Sunday.
news.head: Tetairoa McMillan leads Panthers receivers in win
news.impact: McMillan's ten targets led the team, with Jalen Coker falling close behind with nine. It's a bummer he didn't connect on more than five, as he could have had a much bigger day. He and Coker are forming a formidable receiving duo in Carolina, and both are startable every week.

news.body: Tetairoa McMillan hauled in five of his eight targets for 75 yards in the Panthers' 59-37 Week 1 loss to the Chicago Bears.
news.head: Tetairoa McMillan hauls in five receptions in Week 1 loss
news.impact: McMillan made the most of his sizeable volume in the Carolina passing attack, finishing second in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the loss. The wideout remains one of the more dynamic pass-catching options in the Carolina offense moving forward, with a Week 2 contest against the Atlanta Falcons up next.

news.body: Tre Tucker recorded four receptions on five targets for 41 yards in the Raiders loss to the Patriots. He lost six yards on two rushes in the lost.
news.head: Tre Tucker hauls in four passes in Week 5
news.impact: Tucker led the wide receiver group in targets, but fell behind Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty in receptions and yardage. Tucker is likely a volatile option in a Week 6 matchup with Buffalo.

news.body: Tre Tucker caught four of his eight targets for 44 yards in a 30-27 loss to the Chiefs in Week 4.
news.head: Tre Tucker goes for 44 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Tucker tied for third on the team with his eight targets in a game where Kirk Cousins attempted 52 passes. Tucker has been a solid fantasy option this season, posting 15 catches for 233 yards and a touchdown through four games. He will be a fantasy flex in Week 5 vs. the Patriots.

news.body: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-4 targets for 43 yards in the Raiders 35-27 win over the Saints on Sunday.
news.head: Tre Tucker hauls in four passes Sunday
news.impact: Tucker led Raiders wide receivers in receptions and yards. Still his upside remains limited for fantasy managers.

news.body: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-7 targets for 119 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-14 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.
news.head: Tre Tucker stellar in win Sunday
news.impact: The Raiders were able to pick up an upset win over the Chargers on Sunday, and Tucker played a big part in that. He led the team in receptions and yards over the course of the afternoon, and he also caught a touchdown, which further helped his fantasy total. He will likely have other big games moving forward, but they will be inconsistent and hard to predict, especially with Brock Bowers (knee) soon to return to the lineup.

news.body: Treylon Burks caught two of his five targets for 26 yards in the Commanders' 27-27 tie against the New York Giants in Week 5.
news.head: Treylon Burks quiet in Week 5
news.impact: Burks remains one of many non-factors in the Washington passing attack to begin the season, finishing with under 50 receiving yards in each of his four contests. The wideout can be left off rosters in all formats ahead of a Week 6 contest against the San Francisco 49ers.

news.body: Treylon Burks (shoulder) logged a full practice session on Thursday.
news.head: Treylon Burks (shoulder) logs full practice Thursday
news.impact: As expected, Burks was able to log another full practice session on Thursday. His shoulder injury isn't serious and he is expected to play through it this week, and he may see more work than usual against the Giants with Terry McLaurin (hamstring) and Stefon Diggs (hamstring) both at risk of being sidelined for that matchup.

news.body: Treylon Burks (shoulder) fully practiced for the Commanders on Wednesday.
news.head: Treylon Burks (shoulder) fully practices Wednesday
news.impact: Burks was dealing with some kind of a shoulder injury following Week 4, but it's not a serious issue and didn't prevent him from logging a full practice this week. Look for him to continue to contribute on this offense moving forward, though he won't have much fantasy value for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Treylon Burks caught 1-of-3 targets for 47 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders loss to the Colts.
news.head: Treylon Burks finds the end zone in Week 4
news.impact: Burks caught the first touchdown of rookie QB Athan Kaliakmanis' career, the lone touchdown for the Commanders' offense Sunday. Fantasy managers should still view Burks as an option only in deeper leagues.

news.body: Tyreek Hill’s agent Drew Rosenhaus said he remains in talks with multiple NFL teams.
news.head: Tyreek Hill remains in talks with multiple teams
news.impact: Hill continues to rehab his surgically repaired knee. Rosenhaus added that “nothing is imminent at this time.” He remains without a clear timetable to sign and return.

news.body: Tyreek Hill is expected to sign with a team in the coming days, per his agent. He’s been linked to the Chiefs, but other teams are in the mix.
news.head: Tyreek Hill expected to sign in the coming days
news.impact: Hill could give the Chiefs some depth, but it will be interesting to see how much of an impact he could make at this stage of his career while also coming off of a major knee injury. He’s worth stashing, but keep expectations low.

news.body: Tyreek Hill is not expected to sign with a team before the season begins, according to his agent Drew Rosenhaus.
news.head: Tyreek Hill not expected to sign before Week 1
news.impact: Hill has been on the long road to recovery after sustaining a major knee injury in Week 4 last season, and it looks like he will remain a free agent when the 2026 season begins. However, the 32-year-old could receive interest from contenders as the season goes on if he continues to progress in his rehab.

news.body: Tyreek Hill says that he still has “no power” in his left leg that he injured early on in 2025 while playing for the Miami Dolphins. The free agent receiver still has a ways to go before playing football again.
news.head: Tyreek Hill says he still has ‘no power’ in left leg
news.impact: Hill suffered a gruesome knee dislocation and multiple ligament tears in Week 4 of 2025, missing the rest of the season. It’s a big blow to his chances of finding a team and making his way back onto the field in 2026, especially if he is still struggling to find power in his injured leg. More than likely he will miss the majority of 2026, and its possible he will not see the field again until 2027.

news.body: Wan'Dale Robinson caught 6-of-7 targets for 53 yards in the Titans 26-3 loss against the Texans on Sunday.
news.head: Wan'Dale Robinson leads Titans in receiving Sunday
news.impact: Robinson posted his third game with 50 yards on the season. He remains a WR3/ flex play next week against the Colts.

news.body: Wan'Dale Robinson caught 3-of-5 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Titans loss to the Ravens.
news.head: Wan'Dale Robinson hauls in three passes in Week 4
news.impact: Robinson caught the lone touchdown pass from Cam Ward against the Ravens, giving Robinson a touchdown in back-to-back games. The 25-year-old will look to continue that streak in Week 5 against the Texans.

news.body: Wan'Dale Robinson caught 7-of-11 targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 12-7 loss to the New York Giants.
news.head: Wan'Dale Robinson finds end zone Sunday
news.impact: Robinson played well against his former team on Sunday. He led the team in targets and receptions against the Giants, and he also scored the team's only touchdown over the course of the afternoon. Despite the good game, fantasy managers should not consider him a viable option moving forward.

news.body: Wan'Dale Robinson caught his lone target for a nine-yard gain in a 24-20 loss to the Eagles in Week 2.
news.head: Wan'Dale Robinson held to one catch in Week 2
news.impact: Robinson was quiet in what was almost an upset win over the Eagles. The Titans only passed for 183 yards in the contest with Elic Ayomanor leading the way. Through two games in Tennessee, Robinson has caught six of his seven targets for 47 scoreless yards. He will need to see more frequent work moving forward to be trustworthy in fantasy. The Titans will face the Giants in Week 3.

news.body: Xavier Hutchinson caught 4-of-5 targets for 65 yards in the Texans 26-3 win over the Titans.
news.head: Xavier Hutchinson totals team-high 65 yards Sunday
news.impact: Hutchinson led Houston in receiving on the afternoon. He still remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

news.body: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-5 targets for 46 yards in the Texans 34-30 loss against the Cowboys.
news.head: Xavier Hutchinson sees five targets Sunday
news.impact: Hutchinson made the most of his playing time despite seeing just 16 snaps. He remains off the fantasy radar in his current role.

news.body: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-6 targets for 51 yards in a 19-17 loss to the Colts.
news.head: Xavier Hutchinson hauls in three passes in Week 3 loss
news.impact: Hutchinson was expected to step into a larger role with Nico Collins (hamstring) out of the lineup. The Houston offense struggled as a whole against the Colts and will look to pick up their first win of the season against Dallas in Week 4.

news.body: Xavier Hutchinson caught 3-of-9 targets for 37 yards in the Texans 20-6 loss against the Bengals on Sunday.
news.head: Xavier Hutchinson sees nine targets Sunday
news.impact: With Nico Collins sidelined, Hutchinson led Houston in targets. It did not lead to much production. He could be in the streaming conversation in deeper leagues next week if Collins remains sidelined.

news.body: Xavier Worthy caught four of his seven targets for 70 yards in a 30-27 win over the Raiders in Week 4.
news.head: Xavier Worthy goes for 70 yards in Week 4
news.impact: Worthy got some extra looks with Rashee Rice injuring his hamstring during the game. The veteran did most of his damage on a 41-yard catch from Patrick Mahomes II. With Week 4 being by far his best game of the season, Worthy will look to stay hot in Week 6 against the Chargers after his Week 5 bye.

news.body: Xavier Worthy caught both of his targets for 20 yards in the Chiefs' 24-10 Week 3 win over the Miami Dolphins.
news.head: Xavier Worthy quiet in Week 3 win
news.impact: Worthy was bottled up by a surprising Miami defensive effort Sunday, finishing with less than three receptions for the first time in three contests. The wideout has struggled to offer fantasy managers a reliable pass-catching option to begin the season, with a Week 4 contest against the Las Vegas Raiders up next.

news.body: Xavier Worthy caught 5-of-7 targets for 25 yards and a touchdown in Sunday night's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts.
news.head: Xavier Worthy finds end zone in overtime win Sunday
news.impact: Worthy saw good involvement with seven targets on Sunday night, although he was only able to turn that into five catches for 25 yards against the Colts. He was able to score on one of those catches, however, which salvaged his night from a fantasy perspective. He should not be considered a strong option at the wide receiver position until we see some more consistent production from him.

news.body: Xavier Worthy caught 3-of-6 targets for 18 yards in Monday night's 31-10 win over the Denver Broncos.
news.head: Xavier Worthy quiet in win Monday
news.impact: Worthy was Kansas City's most targeted player on Monday night, but he wasn't able to do much with his opportunities, finishing with just three catches for 18 yards against the Broncos. He isn't expected to be a relevant fantasy option for the foreseeable future.

news.body: Zay Flowers came up with 8-of-9 targets for 53 yards in Sunday's 30-23 OT win over the Falcons.
news.head: Zay Flowers grabs eight passes for the second straight week
news.impact: Flowers now has 16 grabs on 19 targets over the last two weeks, as he remains a PPR mainstay for fantasy managers. He did miss a game back in Week 2, but in the four that he's played, the fourth-year receiver has averaged 6.5 receptions for more than 100 yards. Flowers is a WR2 at worst in standard fantasy formats right now.

news.body: Zay Flowers (foot) is officially active for Week 5 for the Baltimore Ravens against the Atlanta Falcons.
news.head: Zay Flowers (foot) active for Week 5
news.impact: Flowers is good to go after passing through pregame warmups without any issues for head coach Jesse Minter, providing the Baltimore passing attack with an explosive pass-catching option against the Falcons Sunday night.

news.body: Zay Flowers (foot) is expected to play on Sunday against the Falcons and push through his foot injury.
news.head: Zay Flowers (foot) expected to play on Sunday
news.impact: If Flowers suits up, he will provide backup QB Tyler Huntley with a more than capable target downfield in a Ravens passing attack that lacks much punch behind him. He will be needed to prevent the offense from being one-dimensional, especially with the Falcons offense picking up steam since the return of Michael Penix.

news.body: Zay Flowers is listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the Falcons.
news.head: Zay Flowers (foot) listed questionable Sunday
news.impact: Flowers was limited in practice all week. He should be on the favorable side of questionable.
